front: How long is an IPv6 address, and how is it written?
back: 128 bits: eight 16-bit groups, each written as four hexadecimal digits.

front: Why may an IPv6 address contain :: only once?
back: With two ::, nobody could tell how many zero groups each one replaces.

front: Two zero runs are equally long. Which one does canonical IPv6 text replace with ::?
back: The leftmost. A single zero group is written as 0, never as ::.

front: Which prefix holds global unicast addresses?
back: 2000::/3, so the first hex digit is 2 or 3. These are the publicly routable addresses.

front: What are the three parts of a typical global unicast address?
back: Global routing prefix (often /48), 16-bit subnet ID, 64-bit interface ID.

front: Which block is unique local, and how do its addresses start in practice?
back: fc00::/7; addresses in use start fd. They are private: routed inside an organization, not on the Internet.

front: Which prefix marks a link-local address, and how far does it reach?
back: fe80::/10. It works on one link only; routers never forward it. Every IPv6 interface has one.

front: Why must you name an interface when you ping a link-local address from a router?
back: The same fe80:: address can exist on every link, so the address alone does not say which link to use.

front: IPv6 has three address types. Which are they, and which IPv4 type is missing?
back: Unicast, anycast and multicast. There is no broadcast; multicast does that work.

front: What is an anycast address?
back: One unicast address assigned to several devices. Routing delivers each packet to one of them, normally the nearest. No prefix identifies it.

front: Which multicast groups mean all nodes and all routers on a link?
back: ff02::1 is all nodes; ff02::2 is all routers. Every multicast address begins ff (ff00::/8).

front: How do you form a solicited-node multicast address?
back: Append the address's last 24 bits to ff02::1:ff00:0/104. An address ending 12:3456 gives ff02::1:ff12:3456.

front: What do ::1 and :: mean?
back: ::1 is the loopback address, the device itself. :: is the unspecified address, used as a source before a host has an address.

front: What is 2001:db8::/32 reserved for?
back: Documentation and lab examples. It is never routed on the Internet.

front: How many /64 prefixes fit in a /56?
back: 2^(64 − 56) = 256. The eight borrowed bits are the last two hex digits of the fourth group.

front: Which /60 network contains 2001:db8:5:c7f2::1?
back: 2001:db8:5:c7f0::/60. A /60 keeps three hex digits of the fourth group; zero everything after them.

front: Why do IPv6 LANs use a /64 prefix?
back: SLAAC adds a 64-bit interface ID to the advertised prefix, and the two must total 128 bits.

front: How is a modified EUI-64 interface ID built from a MAC address?
back: Split the MAC in half, insert fffe in the middle, and flip the seventh bit of the first byte.

front: In modified EUI-64, what does a first MAC byte of 00 become? A first byte of 02?
back: 00 becomes 02, and 02 becomes 00. The seventh bit is flipped, not always set.

front: Name the four main Neighbor Discovery messages and their ICMPv6 types.
back: Router Solicitation 133, Router Advertisement 134, Neighbor Solicitation 135, Neighbor Advertisement 136.

front: What does IPv6 use instead of an ARP request and reply?
back: A Neighbor Solicitation sent to the target's solicited-node multicast address, answered by a Neighbor Advertisement carrying the MAC address.

front: How does a host build its address with SLAAC?
back: It takes the /64 prefix from a Router Advertisement and adds its own 64-bit interface ID. No DHCP server is involved.

front: Where does an IPv6 host learn its default gateway automatically?
back: From the Router Advertisement: the gateway is the RA's link-local source address. DHCPv6 has no default-gateway option.

front: What do the M and O flags in a Router Advertisement tell a host?
back: M: get the address from DHCPv6. O: get other settings, such as DNS, from DHCPv6. The default gateway still comes from the RA.

front: What does Duplicate Address Detection check, and how?
back: That no other device on the link has the new address. The host sends a Neighbor Solicitation for it from source ::; no reply means unique.

front: What does ipv6 unicast-routing do on an IOS router?
back: Makes it an IPv6 router: it forwards IPv6 packets between interfaces and sends Router Advertisements. It is off by default.

front: How do ipv6 enable and ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:2::/64 eui-64 differ?
back: ipv6 enable creates only a link-local address. The eui-64 command also creates a global address: your prefix plus an interface ID from the MAC.

front: Which interface command makes a router interface get its address by SLAAC?
back: ipv6 address autoconfig. The interface builds its address from the prefix in another router's RA.
